top_choice_rationale: P001 (B048, Melitz and Helpman) is a distinct, identifiable discovery: selection of heterogeneous firms into exporting and reallocation across firms as a channel for the gains from trade. Melitz (2003) is the originating model and Helpman's exporting-versus-FDI work with Melitz and Yeaple is the natural second credit. Its qualitative predictions (exporter premia, selection, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years, and the idea has spread into macro, growth and development. It is distinct from the 2008 prize for trade theory with representative firms. The main reservation is priority for Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, who are outside the slate. A citation limited to the selection and reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework addresses it only partly, but it does not make the award unwarranted. Welfare-gain magnitudes depend on functional form, so the citation should rest on the qualitative mechanism. I rank it above no award because it meets the common criteria of achievement, maturity and attribution.
recusal_note: No tie to Melitz or Helpman is documented in my profile. My research on reallocation, misallocation and creative destruction is adjacent to the B048 mechanism, so I may be biased toward it. I also co-author with Klenow and Aghion, and I am a frequent co-author of Krusell and a co-author of Hassler, with IIES ties to both. None is a credited candidate on P001. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
